heuristics: The 256-bit fingerprint is a randomized linear map over Z/2^64 lanes; its collision bound is proved for every fixed pair of elements from the uniform masks, and collisions are resolved by exact comparison of the full 576-byte elements, so they cannot produce a wrong output.

The probability that more than 2^40 exact comparisons are needed is at most 2^-38 by Markov and is charged unconditionally; that term is the only subtraction from the exact covered-exponent count m^2/r.
limitations: Analytic construction; no production-size execution or independent qualification.
The declared 2^137-byte storage is mandatory for this construction and is reported as a supplementary bound with no scalar contribution.
Generic square-root attack with an exact join; it does not exploit pairing structure beyond the admissible fixed-Q reduction and makes no security-level claim.
